article.title: Crowds throng New Delhi and wave Indian flags amid escalating protests
article.summary:
Crowds throng New Delhi and wave Indian flags amid escalating proteststoggle caption i Vipin/APNEW DELHI — Thousands of Indians thronged a bustling thoroughfare in the heart of the capital, waving the national flag and demanding the resignation of the country's election chief, the latest show of public dissent against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.
Protesters spanning generations joined the rally, reflecting broad public anger and intensifying pressure on the country's top election official.
Police detained Dipke, the founder of the "Cockroach" movement, ahead of the demonstrations.
He had urged supporters unable to travel to New Delhi to raise the flag and demonstrate in their own communities.
Sponsor MessageThe "Cockroach" movement began as an online satirical campaign this summer after India's chief justice compared unemployed young people to parasites.

article.title: Iraq parliament approves al-Zaidi’s cabinet amid growing economic concerns
article.summary:
Iraq’s parliament has completed the formation of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government after lawmakers approved previously vacant cabinet posts and three deputy prime ministers, including one who is under US sanctions.
Lawmakers voted on Thursday, approving 11 portfolios, including Nayef al-Shammari as defence minister, Yasir al-Maliki as interior minister, a planning minister, a culture minister and a minister of higher education and scientific research.
Lawmakers also approved three deputy prime ministers, including Laith al-Khazali, a senior leader of the Iran-backed Asaib Ahl al-Haq movement and brother of the group’s leader, Qais al-Khazali.
In a statement following the cabinet approval, al-Zaidi thanked parliament and called upon his fellow deputy prime ministers and ministers to “fulfil their responsibilities with the highest levels of commitment, competence and integrity”.
Al-Zaidi added that the state needs about 10 trillion dinars ($6.7bn) monthly to cover salaries and critical spending.

article.title: Albanian PM blames ‘foreign hands’ for unrest as student protests intensify
article.summary:
Riot police clash with protesters for fourth day, as young Albanians protest corruption and poor university conditionsShare Albanian PM blames ‘foreign hands’ for unrest as student protests intensify on social mediaAlbanian Prime Minister Edi Rama has blamed “foreign hands” for the increasingly violent student-led protests that are calling on him to resign.
“This is not a student phenomenon,” Rama said in a video address on Friday.
He said there were “foreign hands that do not wish for Albania to be at peace”.
Protesters hurled bricks and concrete blocks at the education ministry on Tuesday.
Rama won a fourth term last year on promises to take Albania into the EU, aiming for membership as early as 2028.
